items.topic: Should the redundant normalization in Create be cleaned up?
items.context: The Create handler calls normalizeCreateBacklogItemRequest() which uppercases effort (line 121-128), then later calls validateEffort() which also uppercases (line 339). This is harmless but redundant. The batch create handler only uses normalizeCreateRequest (via a different proto message), so its path is clean.

options.label: Yes — remove the duplicate normalization
options.rationale: Cleaner code, single responsibility. validateEffort already handles normalization.

options.label: No — leave as-is (defense in depth)
options.rationale: Redundant normalization is harmless and provides safety if one path changes.

items.context: TestUpdate_WithEffort exists but sends already-uppercase effort. There's no test verifying that a lowercase effort in an update request gets normalized to uppercase. This is a gap — the update handler does normalize (line 517-523) but it's untested for the lowercase case.

options.label: Yes — add TestUpdate_EffortNormalizesCase
options.rationale: Matches the existing create-path test pattern. Verifies the normalization works end-to-end for updates.

options.label: No — the unit test for validateEffort covers this
options.rationale: validateEffort is already tested indirectly; a handler-level test is redundant.

items.text: All 9 existing effort-related tests pass (create, update, batch create — valid, invalid, optional, case normalization). The effort field uses t-shirt sizes (XS, S, M, L, XL) with proto-level validation requiring uppercase and Go-level normalization converting lowercase input before proto validation.

The proto schema enforces effort values via buf.validate 'in' constraint (uppercase only). The Go normalization layer ensures case-insensitive input works by uppercasing before proto validation runs. Without the Go normalization, lowercase effort values would be rejected by proto validation.
